questions.question: During a practice session in a stadium an athlete runs along a circular track and her performance is observed by her coach standing at point on the circle and also by her physiotherapist standing at the centre of the circle. The coach finds that she covers an angle of 72° in 1 min. what will be the angle covered by her in 1 second according to the measurement made by her physiotherapist?

options.text: It depends on the position of the coach on the circular track

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6961176d393c8c0b9ba3a070ab5013bdd71fa57a9826d3a3b156eb03f1f51abc.png] 

Let the athlete runs from A to B in 1 minute and the coach and the physiotherapist observe him from point C and P respectively

Given, ∠ACB = 72°

The angle subtended by the arc at the centre is double of the angle subtended by the arc at a point on the circle.

⇒ ∠APB = 2 × 72 = 144°

Hence, according to physiotherapist the athlete covers an angle of 144° per minute

∴ In 1 second, the angle covered by the athlete according to physiotherapist = 144/60 = 2.4°

questions.question: The radii of two concentric circles are x cm and 26 cm. P and S are the points on larger circle and Q and R are points on smaller circle. If PQRS is a straight line and QR = 40 cm and PS = 48 cm, then what is the value of x? (x < 26 cm)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radii of the two concentric circles are x cm and 26 cm.

PQRS is a straight line and QR = 40 cm and PS = 48 cm, where P and S are the points on a larger circle and Q and R are points on a smaller circle.

**Concept Used:**

The perpendicular drawn from the center of the circle to the chord bisects the chord into two equal parts.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/302c30074160e7c22dae98f7c2452838ce5dff4ed4e5ba6569acafa8b1d661f5.png] 

Construct a perpendicular OT from the center to the straight line PQRS.

In a bigger circle, PS is the chord with a length of 48 cm.

OT is perpendicular to PS 

SO, PT = ST = 24 cm

In △OTP,

OP = 26 cm (Radius)

PT = 24 cm

Using Pythagoras' theorem,

OT² = OP² - PT²

⇒ OT² = 26²- 24²

⇒ OT2 = 676 - 576

⇒ OT2 = 100

⇒ OT = 10 cm

In a smaller circle, QR is the chord with a length of 40 cm.

OT is perpendicular to QR

SO, QT = RT = 20 cm

In △OTQ,

OQ = x cm (Radius)

QT = 20 cm

OT = 10 cm

Using Pythagoras' theorem,

OQ2 = OT2 + QT2

⇒ OQ2 = 20² + 102

⇒ OQ2 = 400 + 100

⇒ OQ2 = 500

⇒ OQ = 10√ 5 cm

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: AB is 12 cm long chord of a circle with centre O and radius 10 cm. The tangents at A and B intersect at P. What is the length of OP?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 12 cm

Radius = 10 cm

The tangents at A and B intersect at P.

**Concept used:**

**AAA similarity:** If all three angles in one triangle are the same as the corresponding angles in the other, then the triangles are similar.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4342df0d3a229c6831f5e01077e9458c5db4f4381e9dd4d109c1a502860a2803.png] 

AB is the chord of the circle with centre O

Now,

OP ⊥ AB

So, OP bisects AB

AL = BL = 6 cm

Also,

OL = √(OA)² – (AL)²

⇒ OL = √(10)² – (6)²

⇒ OL = √100 – 36

⇒ OL = √64

⇒ OL = 8 cm

Now,

In ΔOAP and ΔOLA

∠OAP = ∠OLA

OA = OB = 10 cm (Radius)

OL = OL [Common]

So, ΔOAP ~ ΔOLA 

⇒ OP/OA = OA/OL [Corresponding sides are proportional]

⇒ OP/10 = 10/8

⇒ 8 OP = 100

⇒ OP = (100/8) cm

⇒ OP = 12.5 cm

**∴ The length of OP is 12.5 cm**

questions.question: PQ is the diameter of a circle with centre O. PT is a tangent touching the circle at P. The secant QT intersects the circle at S. O and S are joined. If ∠SOP = 104°, what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠PTQ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

PQ is the diameter of a circle with centre O. PT is a tangent touching the circle at P. The secant QT intersects the circle at S. O and S are joined. If ∠SOP = 104º, what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠PTQ?

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c581ff64ab215cb3b068be69bcc671b3ba604eb6825f6cdfedce02e422b4d04b.png] 

∠OQS = ∠OSQ Since, (OS = OQ (radius)

But ∠SOP = ∠OQS + ∠OSQ (Exterior angle theorem)

104° = 2 ∠OQS

∠OQS = 52°

In Tringle QPT

∠PTQ = 180° - ∠OQS - ∠QPT

∠PTQ = 180°- 52° - 90°

∠PTQ = 38°

Therefore, ∠PTQ = 38°

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: The perimeter of a sector of a circle of radius 7.4 cm is 20.6 cm. The area of this sector is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of circle = 7.4 cm

Perimeter of a sector = 20.6 cm

**Formula used:**

Perimeter of sector = 2r + (2 × π × r × θ)/360°

Area of a sector = (π × r² × θ)/360°

**Calculation:**

Perimeter of sector = 2r + (2 × π × r × θ)/360°

⇒ 20.6 = 2 × 7.4 + (2 × π × 7.4 × θ)/360°

⇒ 20.6 - 14.8 = (2 × π × 7.4 × θ)/360°

questions.question: The chord of a circle is equal to its radius. The angle (in degrees) subtended by this chord at any point on the minor arc of the circle is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The chords of a circle = radius of the circle

**Concept used:**

The angle of an equilateral triangle = 60°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be2bdeec80d53e4a8ce034529d6fb1351816e3b4c859c64d2ad2b4584cf14852.png] 

In the figure:

OD = OE = radius

DE = OD = OE

So, △DOE is an equilateral triangle.

∠DOE = 60°

⇒ ∠DQE = (∠DOE/2)

⇒ 60/2 = 30°

DQEP is a cyclic quadrilateral.

∠DQE + ∠DPE = 180°

⇒ 30 + ∠DPE = 180

⇒ ∠DPE = 180 - 30

⇒ ∠DPE = 150°

**∴ The correct answer is 150°.**
